{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-or-c","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"1297c048a750d4daa26f7a2926075ecf8bf08496e3f3c366056f39f1271e28db","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-or-class-c:lineage:46","source_registry_sha256":"ce8335c1d96ff7ed209bf236ba9a56fe92dfebd915bc0e2fa7fb830ee03f0f09","source_liveness_sha256":"c4da479589e7933e4eef7366086dfcc48a420303d0089cb0ea19ad9137abec1d"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Other important information: Class C privilege, application requirements, proof documents, card designations, insurance and collision duties","heading":"C2 — Collision reporting, unattended vehicles and loss of privileges plus confusables: permit versus license age, practice-hour paths, document expiry windows, insurance amounts and report triggers","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — Collision reporting, unattended vehicles and loss of privileges plus confusables: permit versus license age, practice-hour paths, document expiry windows, insurance amounts and report triggers
Continuation facts for collision reporting, unattended vehicles and loss of privileges followed by confusable pairs, each tied to one manual page; knowledge-graph hints (group, difficulty, confusable pair) sit only in the trailing Why it matters line of each block.

FACT_ID: sec11-R01 | anchor: A06
You must file a collision report on Form 735-32 within 72 hours when damage to the vehicle you were driving is over $2,500, or damage to property other than a vehicle is over $2,500. [A06]
Why it matters: group collision reports; continuation; difficulty hard.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec11-R02 | anchor: A06
A collision report is also required within 72 hours when any vehicle has more than $2,500 of damage and any vehicle is towed from the scene because of collision damage. [A06]
Why it matters: group collision reports; continuation; difficulty hard.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec11-R03 | anchor: A06
A collision report is also required whenever the collision causes injury or death. [A06]
Why it matters: group collision reports; continuation; difficulty medium.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec11-R04 | anchor: A06
A vehicle owner must file the collision report when the owner's vehicle was in a reportable collision and the driver fails to report it. [A06]
Why it matters: group collision reports; continuation; difficulty medium.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec11-R05 | anchor: A06
A police report does not replace your duty to file your own collision report with DMV. [A06]
Why it matters: group collision reports; confusable police report versus DMV report; difficulty hard.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec11-R06 | anchor: A06
If you hit an unoccupied vehicle, try to find its owner, and if you cannot, leave a note with your name, address and a short account of what happened. [A06]
Why it matters: group unattended vehicles; continuation; difficulty medium.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec11-R07 | anchor: A06
Damaging something that is not a motor vehicle carries the same duty: look for its owner or whoever is in charge of it and tell them about the damage. [A06]
Why it matters: group unattended property; continuation; difficulty easy.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec11-R08 | anchor: A07
Keeping your driving privilege depends on keeping a good driving record. [A07]
Why it matters: group loss of privileges; continuation; difficulty easy.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec11-R09 | anchor: A07
You can lose your driving privilege for driving under the influence of alcohol, drugs or inhalants, for failing to report a collision, or for driving uninsured. [A07]
Why it matters: group loss of privileges; continuation; difficulty medium.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec11-R10 | anchor: A07
Too many traffic convictions, handled through the Driver Improvement Program, and failing to comply with court fines can also cost you your privilege, and the manual says its list is not complete. [A07]
Why it matters: group loss of privileges; continuation; difficulty medium.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec11-R11 | anchor: A01
The instruction permit age is 15, while the driver license age is 16. [A01]
Why it matters: group application; confusable permit age versus license age; difficulty easy.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0097]

FACT_ID: sec11-R12 | anchor: A02
A teen applicant reaches the practice requirement either with 100 supervised hours alone, or with 50 supervised hours combined with an ODOT-approved traffic safety education course. [A02]
Why it matters: group teen requirements; confusable hours-only path versus course path; difficulty hard.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0098]

FACT_ID: sec11-R13 | anchor: A02
The teen permit must be held at least 6 months, while the practice supervisor must be at least 21 and licensed for at least 3 years. [A02]
Why it matters: group teen requirements; confusable permit period versus supervisor rules; difficulty medium.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0098]

FACT_ID: sec11-R14 | anchor: A03
An expired Oregon license, permit or ID card can still prove identity for up to 13 years after expiry, while an expired out-of-state card counts for only up to 1 year. [A03]
Why it matters: group proof documents; confusable Oregon card versus out-of-state card; difficulty hard.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec11-R15 | anchor: A05
The minimum liability limits are $25,000 for injury to one person and $50,000 for two or more people per collision, while the separate property damage minimum is $20,000. [A05]
Why it matters: group insurance; confusable bodily injury versus property damage minimums; difficulty hard.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec11-R16 | anchor: A05
Personal Injury Protection is set at $15,000 per person, while Uninsured Motorist Coverage is set at $25,000 per person and $50,000 per collision. [A05]
Why it matters: group insurance; confusable personal injury protection versus uninsured motorist; difficulty hard.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec11-R17 | anchor: A04
A veteran designation requires a discharge document as proof, while a deaf or hard of hearing designation requires no proof at all. [A04]
Why it matters: group card designations; confusable veteran versus hearing designation; difficulty medium.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0100]
